text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: GeoDNS / external resolver errors detected for eu-west edge. Elevated SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN rates since 12:03 UTC. Affected hostnames: inference.redwood.ai (eu routing), embeddings.redwood.ai (eu). Monitoring shows spike in DNS failures and increased client-side retries. Auto-alerting to #incidents and paging oncall.

sre_elaine: ack — I'm taking this. Starting initial triage: grabbing resolver logs + repro from EU vantage. Paging network.

network_kevin: seeing similar from our Cloudflare resolver probes. Dig from multiple EU vantage points returns SERVFAIL or inconsistent sets. Route53 health checks for eu endpoints show flapping. Could be propagation / partial outage in one AZ causing GeoDNS to return stale/empty answers.

sre_elaine: quick check (from eu-probe1):
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.redwood.ai A
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.ai A
93.184.216.34
```
So some resolvers get answers, others time out.

customer_ops_maria: we already have ~12 tickets from EU customers with 502s for inference endpoints. Estimated %error of EU traffic ~7% per synthetic checks.

eng_raj: Can we temporarily failover EU traffic to the global US pool (lower latency for some customers but keeps service up)? TTL is 60s, but caches might stick. What's the quick mitigation plan?

network_kevin: plan options:
1) Adjust GeoDNS routing policy to prefer US endpoints for EU region (manual override) — immediate but cache dependent.
2) Add Route53 latency-based failover records pointing to US origin and raise health-check tolerance.
3) Push Cloudflare resolver purge / coordinate with CF support if it's a resolver-side issue.

I'll start with option 1 to reduce customer impact.

sre_elaine: do it and post the exact change. Also increase Route53 health-check interval to avoid flapping false positives while we investigate.

network_kevin: doing manual change now — switching geo policy for eu-west to route to global-primary (US) for host inference.redwood.ai. Updating weights and setting small-step TTL 30s.

incident-bot: :information_source: Action recorded: network_kevin changed GeoDNS routing for inference.redwood.ai (eu-west -> global-primary) at 12:09:02 UTC. Previous TTL 60s -> 30s.

customer_ops_maria: reporting back — ticket volume decreased; new complaints are slower. Still seeing some 502s from mobile carriers in western europe.

sre_elaine: Running synthetic smoke across EU providers. Result: error rate dropped from ~7% -> ~1.8% in last 5 mins. Good improvement but not fully resolved.

eng_raj: Can we also add a targeted config to our client-side retry (shorten backoff to try alternate region quicker)? Might help mobile carriers with long DNS cache times.

sre_elaine: Good idea — rolling a quick client-config bump in hosted API gateway to allow quicker fallback. Pushing patch to canary now.

sre_ash: I will take the on-call for the next 30 minutes. If it degrades again, escalate to network oncall.

network_kevin: Opening a ticket with Cloudflare to check their EU resolver pool — attaching dig traces and timestamps. CF ticket #CF-98231.

manager_oliver: Keep execs updated if customer impact over 15% or more than 30 customers affected. Current impact looks limited.

sre_elaine: Root-cause triage notes so far: inconsistent DNS answers across resolver populations; Route53 health checks flapped possibly due to transient origin reachability in one AZ. Still verifying whether CF or Route53 side caused the propagation/no-answer behavior.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation status: manual GeoDNS failover applied. Error rate reduced to ~1.5% EU. Active monitoring continuing. Next update in 15 minutes or on significant change.

customer_ops_maria: customers with active outages: 3 enterprise customers (support bridge open). CS on bridge with engineering and network.

eng_raj: After we stabilize, we should plan: 1) increase TTL flashback plan, 2) review health-check thresholds and distribution across AZs, 3) run DNS-propagation runbook and contact CF / AWS if needed.

sre_ash: taking responsibility for post-incident follow-up. I'll create the postmortem ticket and include the CF ticket link and Route53 change history. Assigning to network_kevin and eng_raj for root cause analysis.

sre_elaine: current status: monitoring shows steady state, will hand off to sRE on next shift. Leaving note: keep TTL at 30s for 1 hour then revert to 60s once propagation stable. Re-enable original geo policy only after CF confirms resolver pool healthy.

network_kevin: CF responded: they're investigating anomalous packet loss in one EU PoP around 12:00-12:10 UTC. They requested our dig logs — provided. CF suggests waiting for internal stabilization before flipping routes back.

incident-bot: :lock: Post-incident actions created: P1 ticket P-10092 (postmortem), CF-98231 link, Route53-change-log attached. Incident severity: S2 (partial regional impact). Assigned: sre_ash, network_kevin, eng_raj.

manager_oliver: Thanks team. Keep timeline + all commands in the postmortem. If impact creeps up, ping me directly.

sre_ash: handoff complete. I'll monitor for 30m and then close the thread if stable. :thumbsup:

sre_elaine: thanks everyone. Good job getting to mitigation quickly.
